name: IL-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+34 partisan lean makes the seat overwhelmingly Democratic even with Danny Davis retiring
La Shawn Ford's fundraising edge: about $819K raised versus Chad Koppie's $58K and $42 on hand
Polymarket prices the Democratic side at 97%
No public general-election polling; open-seat dynamics add modest margin uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's deep Democratic lean, Ford's overwhelming financial advantage, and markets pricing the Democratic side near 97% make an upset highly implausible; the open seat and absence of polling leave uncertainty only about the size of the margin.
model.watch: Unusually low turnout or a late infusion of outside money for Koppie could narrow the margin, though not plausibly the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Danny Davis (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Illinois's 7th District is among the most Democratic seats in the country, and Danny Davis's retirement does not change its fundamental partisan character. La Shawn Ford enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly $819,000, while Republican Chad Koppie has raised under $59,000 and reported just $42 on hand. Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 97 percent.

No public general-election polling covers the race, and the open seat adds some uncertainty about turnout and margin. Still, the district's D+34 partisan lean, the funding gap, and the absence of serious Republican investment point to an easy Democratic hold. The main open question is the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
